title: Histos Tool Lock 1–2
$comment: Provenance for the imported half of a policy. The policy itself stays a self-contained, hashed artifact and never references a contract it does not contain; this file records where the imported shapes came from and what they looked like when a human last reviewed them. Nothing here affects a decision, so nothing here is part of the policy's content_hash. The hash definitions below are NORMATIVE: a second implementation that computes them differently will report drift the reference engine does not, which is worse than reporting none.

lock_version.description: Format version. Version 2 adds the reviewed source copy; an implementation that does not recognise the value refuses the file rather than reading what it can.

policy.description: File name of the policy these entries belong to. Informational: the pairing is by location on disk, not by this string.

tools.description: One entry per tool that came from an importable source. A policy tool absent here is not verified by a drift check, and a drift report must say so rather than imply coverage it does not have.

schema_sha256.description: NORMATIVE. 'sha256:' + SHA-256 over canonical_json(shape), where `shape` is the per-kind object defined in $defs/shape. Answers: did the declared shape change at all, including in a part the projection discards?

description_sha256.description: NORMATIVE. 'sha256:' + SHA-256 over canonical_json(description), where description is the source's description string or null. Hashed separately because it never reaches a tool contract, and a description is where a tool-poisoning payload hides: 'the contract is unchanged' must never be reported as 'the tool definition is unchanged'. An absent description hashes as JSON null, so absent and empty are distinguishable.

contract_sha256.description: NORMATIVE. 'sha256:' + SHA-256 over canonical_json({"args": <schema fingerprint>, "returns": <schema fingerprint>}) of the projected contract. Answers: did the change reach the part that is enforced? Excludes access, resource constraints, bindings, confirmation, limits and output rules — those are written by a human and adding one is not tool drift.

reviewed.description: The source shape and description a human actually reviewed. Required in version 2 so drift can explain what changed rather than only naming a moved hash.

shape.description: The source shape that was reviewed, or null when the source itself declared no shape. Omitted only when shape appears in elided.

description.description: The source description that was reviewed, including null when it was absent. Omitted only when description appears in elided.

elided.description: Reviewed parts deliberately omitted because they exceeded the lock's bounded evidence size.

kind.description: Which reader produced this entry. Determines the `shape` layout, so an unrecognised kind is refused rather than assumed.

locator.description: Where the definition was read from — an endpoint, a file path, a document URL. Recorded so a drift check can be re-run against the same place; never dereferenced automatically.
